summary: Delayed ACK window causes stale fragment replay on SSE resume
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that after a short network interruption and SSE resume, the streaming session replays stale fragments (duplicate partial text blocks) that appear separated by a ~250ms gap. Impact: downstream application shows duplicate sentences and occasional interleaved metadata events, causing UI confusion and user-facing content duplication. Environment: BrightRide Health dedicated fleet in prod-us-west using gpt-redwood-13b-v1 behind our sse-proxy with client library v2.4.2. Observed since 2026-03-11 18:23 PDT; intermittently ~1-3x per hour on this tenant.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long-running SSE stream (session-id header) using client v2.4.2 against prod-us-west. 2) Allow model to emit >3 choice fragments (simulate ~1.5s cadence). 3) Introduce a short packet-loss event or TCP RST at edge for ~1-2s (simulated via tc/netem or client toggling network). 4) Re-establish network and call resume with last-received-offset from client. 5) Observe resumed stream containing duplicate earlier fragments separated by a short gap and out-of-band meta events.
logs:
Proxy logs (snippet):
[2026-03-11T18:23:45.123Z] session=br-7f2 accept from client 10.1.8.45
[2026-03-11T18:23:47.987Z] session=br-7f2 upstream write stalled (socket EPIPE)
[2026-03-11T18:23:48.001Z] session=br-7f2 client disconnected, resume-token=rtok_XXXX
[2026-03-11T18:23:50.210Z] session=br-7f2 client reconnect resume-token=rtok_XXXX last_offset=4821
[2026-03-11T18:23:50.463Z] session=br-7f2 proxy forwarded resume to serving-runtime
Serving runtime logs (snippet):
[2026-03-11T18:23:50.462Z] resume-request token=rtok_XXXX offset=4821
[2026-03-11T18:23:50.465Z] resume-ack delayed by 260ms due to ack-window flush logic
[2026-03-11T18:23:50.726Z] re-emitting fragments 4808-4832 to session br-7f2
Client trace (customer):
-- Received fragments 4796-4821 (normal)
-- After resume: received 4808-4832 (duplicates for 4808-4821), then fresh fragments 4833-...
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: the sse-proxy uses an acknowledgment batching window to reduce egress calls to serving-runtime. On brief disconnects, the proxy delays sending resume/ack updates for up to ~250-300ms; when the serving-runtime flushes its buffered tokens it replays a range already delivered to the client leading to duplicate fragments. Correlated evidence: replay start aligns with 'resume-ack delayed by 260ms' log in runtime. Reproducible in lab when enabling proxy ack batching and simulating a 1-2s disconnect. Not consistent with client library bug — multiple client versions (v2.4.2 and v2.3.9) reproduced same behavior. Related to previously seen resume offset mismatches (linked SUP-12784) but distinct in that duplicates are contiguous replay rather than truncated final choice. Potential contributing factor: combination of proxy keepalive backoff and runtime's buffered-output flush policy. Next steps: instrument ack-window timers in proxy, add high-resolution spans to resume path, and attempt a forced proxy disable of ack batching for a single tenant to confirm mitigation.
workaround: Short-term mitigation for BrightRide: 1) Disable proxy ack batching for the customer's dedicated prefix (config flag enable_ack_batching=false) — reduces throughput efficiency but prevents delayed replay. 2) Client-side dedupe: include fragment sequence IDs and ignore repeats where sequence <= last_seen. We shipped client-side dedupe guidance to BrightRide as immediate workaround.
resolution: In progress: engineering has a PR to make proxy ack-window configurable per-tenant and to tighten default flush from 300ms->50ms. Target deployment: canary to prod-us-west planned 2026-03-15 pending QA. Post-deploy we'll monitor replay rate and customer-reported duplicates. Follow-up: update streaming resume runbook with detection heuristics and add automated alert when resume-replay ratio > 0.1%.
